title: Hezbollah Rejects Lebanon Ceasefire Deal — 'Absurd, Humiliating'; IDF Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg Killed by Hezbollah ATGM North of Litani — 4 Lebanese Killed in Israeli Strikes — Day 97
detail: Hezbollah formally rejected the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire deal announced on June 3, 2026 on June 4, 2026 (Day 97). Hezbollah's leader publicly called the negotiations 'absurd, humiliating and insulting' and reiterated that Hezbollah will only accept a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon — rejecting the pilot zone framework as insufficient. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun responded by calling the ceasefire deal 'the last chance' for a comprehensive truce. Hours after the ceasefire rejection, IDF Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg, 21, of the 7th Armored Brigade's 75th Battalion, was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) fired at an Israeli tank north of the Litani River — making him the first Israeli soldier killed since the renewed ceasefire had gone into effect that morning. His death underscored the fragility of any Lebanon ceasefire while Hezbollah retained its full military posture. Israeli strikes conducted on June 4 killed 4 Lebanese, adding to the cumulative toll. Washington Post headlined: 'Hezbollah rejects latest ceasefire agreement, Israeli strikes kill 4.' CBS News confirmed Iran's simultaneous declaration of 'no tangible progress' in US-Iran talks, linking the Lebanon failure to the broader diplomatic impasse. NPR: 'Hezbollah rejects ceasefire deal agreed by Israel and Lebanon.'

media.caption: Day 97: Hezbollah rejects Lebanon ceasefire; IDF Capt. Eitan Lemberg killed by ATGM north of Litani River; Israeli strikes kill 4 Lebanese

title: Trump Reveals He Rejected US Plan to Physically Collect Iran's 'Nuclear Dust'; Offers 20-Year Enrichment Moratorium; Open to Meeting Iran's New Supreme Leader — Day 97
detail: President Trump made a series of significant diplomatic disclosures on June 4, 2026 (Day 97). He publicly revealed for the first time that he had rejected a military plan to send US troops into Iran to physically collect enriched uranium — which he described as 'nuclear dust.' Trump said the plan would have taken more than two weeks, required massively airlifted equipment, and he rejected it specifically to avoid a 'Jimmy Carter moment' — a reference to the failed 1980 Iran hostage rescue operation. Trump added that the nuclear material is now 'entombed' and there is 'no reason' to pursue the physical collection option. Trump also signaled he would be open to meeting Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei directly if there is an agreement framework in place — the clearest indication yet of a willingness to pursue summit-level diplomacy. Trump stated he would accept Iran suspending nuclear enrichment for 20 years if Iran made a 'real commitment,' a significant softening from earlier maximalist demands for permanent zero-enrichment. Earlier on June 4, Trump had told CNBC he 'didn't care' about Iran shutting down further talks, calling the process 'very boring.' He later reversed course the same day, claiming a 'very productive call' with Netanyahu and Hezbollah leaders had restarted the pause on mutual attacks and re-enabled US-Iran talks. Iranian FM Araghchi warned that any Israeli strike on Beirut would trigger a 'full-scale resumption' of the Iran-US war. Iran declared 'no tangible progress' in negotiations. Brent crude fell approximately 1% to just below $97/bbl on modestly increased hopes for deal progress following Trump's 20-year moratorium offer.

media.caption: Day 97: Trump reveals rejected 'nuclear dust' plan to collect Iran's enriched uranium; offers 20-year enrichment moratorium; open to meeting Supreme Leader
